matt: Heads-up — after rolling the gpu-operator 1.8.0 chart to prod west-1 we started seeing a subset of nodes advertise GPUs but kubelet shows lower allocatable and scheduling rejects with device-plugin mismatch. pods stuck Pending with `0/48 nodes are available: 48 node(s) didn't match node selector`

sara: ugh can you paste the node and device-plugin logs? is it the nvidia device-plugin or our custom one?

matt: it's the nvidia device-plugin (v0.11.0 -> v0.12.0 upgrade). quick snapshot: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu | wc -l` -> 48 nodes, but `kubectl describe node gpu-node-27` shows `Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu: 0` then later `Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu: 4` (flip-flop).

alex: probably the probe/registration ordering changed in the new operator image — device-plugin registers before NV driver probe finishes, so scheduler sees empty allocatable until driver labels/annotations land. we saw similar reordering in a kubelet upgrade last year.

matt: attaching logs snippet from kubelet on gpu-node-27:
```
Mar 08 14:12:03 kubelet[1234]: device-plugin registration: nvidia-device-plugin v0.12.0 started
Mar 08 14:12:04 kernel: nvidia: probe succeeded for GPU 0
Mar 08 14:12:05 kubelet[1234]: updated capacity: nvidia.com/gpu=4
Mar 08 14:12:05 scheduler: pod-binding failed: no matching node
Mar 08 14:12:06 kubelet[1234]: updated allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu=0  # rollback
Mar 08 14:12:07 device-plugin[5678]: advertise resources
```

sara: that rollback allocatable line is worrying — is something else clearing the allocatable (cgroup or runtime)? any dmesg / driver errors?

matt: dmesg shows a brief `NVRM: GPU XX: failed to initialize on first attempt, retrying` before probe succeeded. suspect driver init race with device-plugin s.Getenv-based probe.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout of gpu-operator/gpu-operator-chart/1.8.0 -> 1.8.1 planned for canary in prod-west-1 at 15:00 UTC :robot_face:

jen: mitigation options for now:
- cordon/evict affected nodes for stable capacity
- pin device-plugin to v0.11.0 in node group helm values and roll back operator if needed
- add a `node.kubernetes.io/driver-ready: "true"` label set by a small init daemon that checks `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` before advertising to k8s

alex: short-term patch we discussed in the infra PR: device-plugin should delay registration until `/sys/bus/pci/devices/*/driver` shows `nvidia`, and add exponential backoff on register to avoid brief advertise then withdraw. I can open PR against our device-plugin fork.

ops-oncall: note — west-1 GPU pool is at 85% commit for dedicated jobs this week, cordoning 10 nodes will push some batch jobs to other regions and increase cross-region egress/cost. we should coordinate with scheduler on capacity-aware spillover before cordoning.

matt: agreed. I'll patch the device-plugin fork with the gated registration today and submit canary to 3 nodes first. will also add a small readiness probe that prevents advertising until driver stable for 30s.

sara: sounds good. also let's add a temporary alert: `gpu.allocatable.flapping` when allocatable changes > 0 for same node within 60s more than 3 times. that will catch regressions before they cascade.

alex: PR 712 merged into our fork with gated registration logic, creating canary helm release `gpu-plugin-canary-1976` to 3 nodes in prod-west-1. monitoring dashboards updated.

infra-bot: canary-deployer: canary rollout started -> nodes: gpu-canary-1,gpu-canary-2,gpu-canary-3. health checks enabled.

matt: monitoring shows stable allocatable on canaries for 12m, no flapping, scheduler can place test pods. starting staged rollout to remaining nodes with 5 node batches.

ops-oncall: FYI we'll also schedule a post-mortem after full rollout to capture root cause and make sure kernel+driver matrix tested in CI. cost impact estimated ~+8% cross-region egress if we had to shift batch load.

jen: nice containment. keep me posted if any canaries fail and we'll hit rollback playbook. :thumbsup:
